issues.legal_issue: A contingent debt secured by property transferred subject to that security forms part of the consideration for the conveyance when calculating ad valorem stamp duty.
material_facts: The sale deed stated that the immovable property was transferred free of encumbrances, but declarations executed by both parties established that the sale was subject to an equitable mortgage over the property.
The mortgage secured a bank guarantee for deferred payments up to a stated limit, and the purchaser was substituted for the seller under the guarantee.

Although the bank had made no payment under the guarantee by the relevant time, the guarantee and mortgage remained in force, and the bank could enforce the mortgage against the transferred property if it had to pay under the guarantee.
issues.conclusion: The contingent liability secured by the mortgage had to be included in the consideration for the sale for stamp-duty purposes; the stamp duty was chargeable on the stated price for the immovable property together with the amount secured by the mortgage.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, including its Explanation, treats a debt or payment obligation to which transferred property is subject, whether actual or contingent, as part of the consideration for an ad valorem conveyance duty. A security for contingent future payments falls within the section. The Court relied on Lord Canning v. Raper, Mortinore v. Inland Revenue Commissioners, Independent Television Authority v. Inland Revenue Commissioners, and Coventry City Council v. Inland Revenue Commissioners. It distinguished Sidhnath Mehrotra v. Board of Revenue and Board of Revenue, Uttar Pradesh v. Rai Saheb Sidhnath Mehrotra because those cases concerned sales free of the relevant encumbrance.

rule.if: stamp_duty_proceeding and property_transferred_subject_to_security and security_covers_contingent_obligation and obligation_enforceable_against_property

predicates.stamp_duty_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the determination of stamp duty chargeable on a property conveyance.
predicates.property_transferred_subject_to_security: The parties transferred the property subject to a security interest over it.
predicates.security_covers_contingent_obligation: The security covers an obligation that may become payable in the future but is not yet ascertained or due.
predicates.obligation_enforceable_against_property: The creditor could enforce the security against the transferred property if the contingent obligation became payable.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty proceeding concerns property transferred subject to security for a contingent obligation enforceable against that property, the contingent obligation is included in the chargeable consideration.
